title: A tidy string toolkit
description:
Write string helpers that handle any Unicode text.

```
reverse("héllo")         -> "olléh"
capitalise("ada lovelace") -> "Ada Lovelace"
is_palindrome("Never odd or even") -> true
count_vowels("Rust is fun") -> 3
```
hints: For `capitalise`, take the first char of each word with `let mut c = w.chars();`, then `c.next()`, and `c.as_str()` gives the rest of the word as a `&str`. `first.to_uppercase()` returns an iterator (a few characters become several), so `collect::<String>()` it.
`c.is_alphanumeric()` is true for letters and digits, so `is_palindrome` can keep only those characters, lower-cased, and compare them with their reverse.
requirements: Each function takes `&str` and returns a new `String` or a value.
stretch: Write `fn wrap(s: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String>` that breaks text into lines without splitting words.
